title: Re-measure fileParallelism: the corruption it works around may be fixed
description:
cloud/factory's vitest config sets fileParallelism: false, so 53 test files run strictly serially. The comment (legacy tick 5qj) records why: the suite runs inside real workerd, and run-workflow.test.ts drives Workflows, Durable Objects and D1 with wall-clock budgets; beside other files on a 2-vCPU runner it failed with hung-context cancellations, 'evicted mid-commit' and 'no such table' - state torn out from under a live test, not code under test.

That was a real observation and the workaround was right. It may also be stale: @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers has isolated storage per test file, and the versions have moved since. This tick is to MEASURE, not to flip the flag: run the suite with fileParallelism on, repeatedly, and see whether the corruption returns.

If it does, record that and leave the flag alone - the 5qj comment gets a date and a version rather than being quietly deleted. If it does not, the serial cost (most of a 345s run) comes back.

The trap to avoid is the one cy2 is about: five tests in this project have already refused innocent work because they sampled timing rather than waiting for it. Turning on parallelism without measuring would manufacture exactly that failure class in a second language.

2026-10-07 16:52 - Re-measured 2026-10-07 on the runtime that moved under the flag (tick 3xe, attempt 4; #203 took the suite from @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers 0.21.3 to 0.22.0, vitest still 4.1.11, and the suite grew 53 -> 80 test files). Method: committed flag untouched, `vitest run --file-parallelism` from the CLI (the override is proven by vitest's Duration line: 1164 s cumulative import in a 171 s parallel wall against 154 s in the 236 s serial run). 20 parallel runs, ALL green — 80 files, 1864 tests, zero failures each — beside two green serial baselines (236 s at host load ~5, 366 s at ~30). Ten parallel runs rode 1-minute host load 13-87, one through the 87 spike: the load-spike condition that failed the 2026-09-18 fifth run, hit ten times, and nothing failed; at that run's 1-in-5 rate, twenty greens is p ~ 1% luck. 'no such table' appeared in none of the 22 runs. Verdict: flag STAYS OFF — it guards the 2-vCPU ubuntu runner where 5qj's corruption was observed, and no laptop run clears CI. Corruption last confirmed: CI, epic 692 (pre-5qj); laptop, 2026-09-18 on pool-workers 0.21.3. Recorded in cloudflare/vitest.config.ts (commit 01456cd2b); the path to flipping it — N parallel runs on the real runner via a temporary workflow_dispatch job — filed as a proposal.
2026-10-07 16:53 - ticfac run epic-t8u: 3xe try 1 (run dispatch #4) merged into epic/t8u as 3b33c07661a6; the integrated gate (go, ts) passed.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded measurement of the suite with fileParallelism enabled, repeated enough times to distinguish a pass from luck. Either the flag is on and the suite is stable across those runs, or it stays off and the comment records the version and date the corruption was last confirmed.
